Brand Guide

Identity guidelines for The 24th Group.

A reference for anyone producing anything under the name — the logo, the palette, the type system, and the handful of interface patterns the site already runs on.

Version 1.0 August 2026 Founder-led venture & operations company
01_Logo

The mark, and the lockup.

A rounded square with a single diamond notch cut from its base — the same shape used as the site's favicon. Paired with the wordmark, set in Oswald, it becomes the lockup.

clear space = mark height, on all sides
Never recolor the markBlack on light grounds, white on dark. No brand-color or gradient fills.
Never add effectsNo drop shadows, bevels, outlines or glow — the flat shape is the point.
Never crowd itRespect the clear space above. Don't set it inside a busy photo without a solid ground behind it.
Assets — logo-lockup-black.png · logo-lockup-white.png · mark-only-black.png
02_Color

Seven colors. Two of them are load-bearing.

Black and white are the system — everything else is used sparingly and only where it means something.

Ink

#050505

Primary text, the mark, dark surfaces.

Paper

#ffffff

The ground. Nearly every page is this.

Grey

#777777

Secondary copy — descriptions, captions.

Soft Accent

#f2efe8

One warm neutral, reserved for the hero card.

Live

#1a8a4a

Status only — a project that's shipped.

In Progress

#c2650c

Status only — a project still being built.

Border

#dedede

Hairlines, card edges, dividers.

Green and orange exist for exactly one job — telling a project's status apart at a glance in the work list. They don't appear as decoration, accents on buttons, or highlights anywhere else.

03_Typography

A tall face for headlines, a quiet one for reading.

Oswald carries every headline on the site — condensed and a little formal, which is what keeps three-word lines like "Culture. Systems. Future." from reading like a slogan. Inter handles everything meant to be read at length.

Aa
Medium500 — card titles Semibold600 — h1 / h2 Bold700 — wordmark only

Oswald · headlines only, tracked tight (−0.01em to −0.025em) at display sizes. Never set in body copy, never below 15px.

Aa
Regular400 — paragraphs Semibold600 — nav, labels Bold700 — status tags

Inter · body copy, navigation, UI labels, captions, tabular data. Default tracking, no tricks.

04_Interface Patterns

The handful of components the site is built from.

There's no separate component library — these are the actual patterns from the live site, reproduced here as reference.

Status tags

Live In progress

Dot + label, tinted background at ~8% of the status color, 1px border at ~20%. border-radius: 6px. The dot is a 6px rounded square, not a circle — it echoes the mark's corner radius rather than being a generic status dot.

Cards

Live

Project name

One or two lines describing what it does, nothing more.

hover me →

border: 1px solid rgba(5,5,5,.08) · radius: 12px · rests with a barely-there shadow, lifts 4px with a soft 32px shadow on hover only when the card is a real link. Non-clickable cards never get the hover treatment — the affordance has to be true.

05_Voice

How the brand actually talks.

Read straight from the site's own copy — three habits worth keeping.

Direct, not clever

Say what the thing is before saying anything else about it.

"Oroko is a structured, canvas-first process mapping tool."

Structural, not decorative

Sections are labelled like a document, not a marketing page — it signals the brand is a system, not a pitch.

01_About  ·  02_The Work

No filler adjectives

Every describing word should be load-bearing. Cut anything that could apply to any company.

"Building culture, infrastructure and technology ventures with clarity, discipline and long-term intent."
